directAnswer: To disable mouse acceleration on Windows 11, open Settings, navigate to Bluetooth & devices > Mouse, click on 'Additional mouse settings', and uncheck 'Enhance pointer precision' under the 'Pointer Options' tab.
summary: Disable mouse acceleration on Windows 11 to achieve more consistent and precise pointer movements, especially useful for gaming and detailed tasks.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.body: Mouse acceleration adjusts the pointer speed based on how quickly you move the mouse, which can affect precision. Disabling it can help maintain consistent control.

sections.heading: Why Disable Mouse Acceleration?
sections.body: For gamers and professionals, disabling mouse acceleration ensures a 1:1 movement ratio, providing more predictable and precise control over the pointer.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.body: If issues arise after disabling mouse acceleration, check for updated mouse drivers and review any third-party software that might override system settings.

steps.title: Open Settings
steps.detail: Press 'Windows + I' to open the Settings app.

steps.title: Navigate to Mouse Settings
steps.detail: Select 'Bluetooth & devices' from the sidebar, then click on 'Mouse'.

steps.title: Access Additional Mouse Settings
steps.detail: Scroll down and click on 'Additional mouse settings'.

steps.title: Disable Enhance Pointer Precision
steps.detail: In the 'Mouse Properties' window, go to the 'Pointer Options' tab and uncheck 'Enhance pointer precision'.

steps.title: Apply Changes
steps.detail: Click 'Apply' and then 'OK' to save your changes.

faqs.question: What is mouse acceleration?
faqs.answer: Mouse acceleration is a feature that increases the speed of the pointer based on how quickly you move the mouse.

faqs.question: Is disabling mouse acceleration beneficial for gaming?
faqs.answer: Yes, many gamers prefer disabling it for consistent and predictable mouse movements.

faqs.question: Can I re-enable mouse acceleration if needed?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can re-enable it by checking 'Enhance pointer precision' in the 'Pointer Options' tab.

caveats: Some third-party mouse software might override these settings.
Changes might not apply if your mouse drivers are outdated.
